answer: A scriptorium keeps one relic manuscript per agent, a hand-inked cipher key that no two copies share. Each epoch the keeper hands the agent a fresh page and a quill, and the agent copies the next cipher fragment from its relic in its own hand, then files the page before the archive bell. Scribes check the page stroke by stroke against the relic, and a copied page fails because no two hands leave the same ink trail. A thousand fake names need a thousand relics and a thousand fresh pages copied by hand before the bell.
